response.sql: WITH gains AS (SELECT ds.raceId, r.circuitId, ds.wins - LAG(ds.wins, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY ds.driverId, r.year ORDER BY r.round) AS gain FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON r.raceId = ds.raceId), per_race AS (SELECT g.raceId, c.country, AVG(g.gain) AS race_avg FROM gains g JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = g.circuitId GROUP BY g.raceId, c.country), country_avg AS (SELECT country, AVG(race_avg) AS avg_wins FROM per_race GROUP BY country), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS bench FROM country_avg), kept AS (SELECT ca.country, ca.avg_wins FROM country_avg ca, benchmark b WHERE ca.avg_wins > b.bench), second AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS m2 FROM kept), final AS (SELECT k.country, k.avg_wins FROM kept k, second s WHERE k.avg_wins > s.m2) SELECT f.country, f.avg_wins AS average, f.avg_wins - b.bench AS above_benchmark, f.avg_wins - s.m2 AS above_second_mean FROM final f, benchmark b, second s ORDER BY f.country;

assumptions.assumption: A driver's 'previous round' is their most recent earlier driverStandings row in the same season (by races.round), not necessarily round minus one. With LAG's default of 0, a driver with no earlier row in that season has their full running wins count as the gain.
Missing values are NULL wins. A NULL wins on the current row, or on an existing earlier row, makes that driver's gain NULL, and AVG skips it. A NULL earlier row is not replaced with 0.

Each race's figure is the average of per-driver gains over all driverStandings rows for that race, including drivers whose gain is 0. Each country's figure is the average of its races' figures, with races counted once each. Countries are grouped by the stored circuits.country text without normalization.
